      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: The telephone number of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20

          pattern: '^[0-9 ()-]*$'

          title: Email address

          type: string
          format: email

## Summary

I implemented the `locality` field for owner creation. When an owner is created, the response now includes `locality` set to `"local"` if their city is the single most common city among existing owners at that moment, otherwise `"remote"`.

Changes made, following the existing `Assign*` pipeline conventions:

1. **`AssignLocality.java`** (new) — the OfficeFloor function. It tallies cities across existing owners (excluding the not-yet-saved owner), finds the single most common city, and sets `locality` to `"local"` only if exactly one city has the max count and it matches the owner's city; otherwise `"remote"`. Ties or an empty owner set → `"remote"`. Cities are grouped case-/whitespace-insensitively via the shared `DuplicateMatching.normalize`, consistent with `NormalizeCity`/`AssignSharesHousehold`.

2. **`owners.POST.yml`** — wired `assignLocality` into the pipeline after `assignSharesHousehold` and before `save` (under the same `transaction` governance). It runs after `normalizeCity`, so the city is already canonicalized.

3. **`Owner.java`** — added a persisted `locality` column with getter/setter (mirroring `sharesHousehold`). Persistence is required because the test reads it back via a subsequent `GET`.

4. **Schema files** (hsqldb, h2, mysql, postgres) — added the `locality VARCHAR(20)` column.

5. **`openapi.yml`** — added the read-only `locality` property to the `Owner` schema, so MapStruct's `OwnerMapper` maps it into the generated `OwnerDto`.

The new `Cp18Tests` acceptance test and the full suite (283 tests) pass.
